# User-triggered fetchers

*Crawler* · also written user-triggered fetcher

Google fetchers that request a page because a user asked for it (for example a site verification), and that generally ignore robots.txt.

**Glossary** (*User-triggered fetchers*): Fetchers that request a page because a user asked for it, such as a translation service. Google's documentation says they generally ignore robots.txt, and Google said AI agents acting for a user fall into the same category.

4 claims mention it: 2 from Google's documentation, 1 shown or said at the event (1 confirmed by Google docs), 1 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [List of Google user-triggered fetchers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/google-user-triggered-fetchers).

- [`D1-C138`](../sessions/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) Docs: Google's page on verifying its crawlers says Googlebot and Google's other common crawlers resolve to crawl-*.googlebot.com or geo-crawl-*.geo.googlebot.com host names, special-case crawlers to rate-limited-proxy-*.google.com and user-triggered fetchers to *.gae.googleusercontent.com or google-proxy-*.google.com, and it publishes each group's IP ranges as JSON files such as common-crawlers.json and special-crawlers.json. `[D1-C138, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/verify-google-requests]`
- [`D2-C122`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Docs: Google says user-triggered fetchers, which fetch a URL because a user asked for it in a Google product (for example Gemini Notebook fetching URLs users add as sources, or Google-Agent acting on a user's request), generally ignore robots.txt rules. `[D2-C122, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/google-user-triggered-fetchers]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C273`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: A community speaker pointed out that, according to Google's documentation, user-triggered fetchers, which fetch a page because a user asked for it, generally ignore robots.txt rules. `[D1-C273, stage, Carlos Ortega, Day 1]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D2-C123`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Analysis: Google documents Gemini grounding only as content from the Search index at prompt time; the live read of a specific page at a user's request, described on stage, is not documented, so it is unclear whether it works like a user-triggered fetcher, which generally ignores robots.txt, or follows Google-Extended. `[D2-C123, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-AIF-05` **MAY** · Documented: Set robots.txt policy per AI crawler by its own token, and know that user-triggered fetchers ignore it (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-IDX-11` **MAY** · Documented: Use the Google-Extended robots.txt token to control Gemini training and grounding (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
